column1: Post‑COVID Inflation & the Monetary Policy Dilemma: An Agent‑Based Scenario Analysis

The thesis titled Post-COVID Inflation & the Monetary Policy Dilemma: An Agent-Based Scenario Analysis by Max Sina Knicker and colleagues explores the complex dynamics of inflation following the COVID-19 pandemic and the challenges faced by monetary policy in addressing these issues. The authors employ the Mark-0 Agent-Based Model to simulate the economic environment from 2020 to 2023  focusing on the behavior of economic agents and their trust in the Central Bank. The study examines the effects of three significant exogenous shocks: a production/consumption shock due to COVID-19 lockdowns  a supply-chain shock  and an energy price shock exacerbated by the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

The research investigates how these shocks influence inflationary dynamics under various monetary policy scenarios  considering factors such as demand-pull  cost-push  and profit-driven inflation. The authors identify four key findings: (i) without effective fiscal policy  the economy may take years to recover or fall into a deep recession
column2: (ii) the success of monetary policy in controlling inflation is largely due to expectation anchoring rather than direct economic impacts of interest rate changes
column3: (iii) strong inflation anchoring can negatively affect consumption and unemployment  creating a narrow window for optimal policy responses due to the trade-off between inflation and unemployment
column4: (iv) wage and price indexation are the most sensitive parameters in the model.

column1: The study's results have significant implications for Central Bank decision-making  providing a tool to anticipate the outcomes of different monetary and fiscal policies. The paper is structured into several sections  beginning with an introduction to the topic and the challenges of inflation prediction post-COVID. It then details the Mark-0 Model  including its approach to inflation expectations and monetary policy. The authors explore various policy channels  such as interest rate adjustments  expectation management  credit regulation  and fiscal measures like helicopter money and windfall taxes.

The paper also discusses the stationary dynamics of the economy without monetary policy intervention and the role of the Central Bank in stabilizing inflation. It models the economic shocks from COVID-19 and their aftermath  analyzing the effects in the absence of stabilization policies and the sensitivity to shock magnitude. The authors then evaluate the monetary policy response to inflationary shocks  considering scenarios with inactive  anchored  and floating expectations  and the sensitivity to policy strength and transmission channels.

The study further examines fiscal stimulus measures  including the effects of helicopter money and windfall taxes  and the dangers of a wage-price spiral. The authors conduct a sloppiness analysis to assess model sensitivity and the risk of hyperinflation spirals. The paper concludes with a summary of findings and their implications for policy-making  emphasizing the importance of expectation management and the careful calibration of monetary and fiscal interventions to navigate the post-COVID economic landscape effectively.
